name: Burg Kronburg
kurzbeschreibung: The ruined hilltop fortress of Burg Kronburg towers over Zams and Schönwies with its pilgrimage church, monastery inn, and valley panoramas.
beschreibung:
Overview

Historic Burg Kronburg perches on a wooded rocky cone at an altitude of 1,082 meters between Zams and Schönwies in the Tyrolean Oberland, high above the Inn Valley. Erected around 1380 by the Lords of Starkenberg with the permission of Tyrolean rulers, the fortress guarded the Upper Inn Valley and controlled vital alpine trade routes for centuries. At the base of the steep castle rock lies the peaceful monastery ensemble of Kronburg, comprising the Maria Hilf pilgrimage church and the traditional Gasthof Kronburg inn. For generations, the complex has served as a spiritual center run by the Sisters of Charity and a serene retreat. Hikers and culture lovers value the prominent crag for its panoramic outlook over the Inn Valley, Lechtal Alps, and the Venet ridge.

Route & Requirements

From Gasthof Kronburg, a shaded woodland path winds up to the ruins on the rocky ridge in about 20 minutes (approx. 100 meters of elevation change). The trail is natural, climbing over stone steps and tree roots, requiring surefootedness and sturdy hiking shoes with treaded soles; the steep approach is impassable for strollers or wheelchairs (the monastery church and inn below are accessible). At the top, the ruins – with their defensive walls and sturdy keep – are preserved and freely open to explore. Wooden stairs lead up to the battlements of the keep, revealing remarkable views of the Inn River and surrounding alpine peaks. Around Kronburg, gentle walking routes such as the path through Kronburg Gorge or the Way of St. James invite relaxing strolls.

Visit & Arrival

Burg Kronburg ruins are freely accessible year-round free of charge; in winter, caution is advised on the rocky path depending on snow and ice conditions. The pilgrimage church is open during daytime hours; Gasthof Kronburg welcomes guests from spring to late autumn with regional specialties. Motorists arrive via the A12 or S16 (exit Zams or Schönwies), following the mountain access road to the parking lot by the monastery. Train travelers arrive at Landeck-Zams station and continue by regional bus or on a one-hour walk.

Tips

Combine your visit to the castle ruins with a peaceful pause in the baroque pilgrimage church and a lunch at Gasthof Kronburg, renowned for fresh regional cooking. A walk through shaded Kronburg Gorge offers refreshing coolness on warm summer days.
dauer: 1.5 to 3 hours (including monastery grounds and gorge)
preis: Castle ruins and pilgrimage church freely accessible free of charge
oeffnungszeiten: Castle ruins and pilgrimage church open year-round; monastery inn open seasonally
